questions.q: What will be the effect on the root mean square velocity of oxygen molecules if the temperature is doubled and oxygen molecule dissociates into atomic oxygen?
options: The velocity of atomic oxygen remains same
The velocity of atomic oxygen doubles
The velocity of atomic oxygen becomes half
The velocity of atomic oxygen becomes four times
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The RMS velocity of a gas is given by, vRMS=3RTM

When O2 dissociates into O its molecular mass becomes M2. Therefore,

Ratio of RMS speed, v1v2=T1T2×M2M1⇒v1v2=T2T×M/2M⇒v2v1=2

questions.q: A polyatomic ideal gas has <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>24</mn></math> vibrational modes. What is the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>γ</mi><mo>?</mo></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Since each vibrational mode has 2 degrees of freedom hence total vibrational degrees of freedom =48

f=3+3+48=54

γ=1+2f=2827=1.03

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
V=2 m3

P=3×106 Pa

PV=nRT

E=f2nRT=f2PV=32×3×106×2

=9×106J

questions.q: To raise the temperature of a certain mass of gas by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> at a constant pressure,<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>160</mn></math> calories of heat is required. When the same mass of gas is cooled by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> at constant volume,<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>240</mn></math> calories of heat is released. How many degrees of freedom does each molecule of this gas have (assume gas to be ideal)?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At constant pressure :

∆Q=nCP∆T ⇒   160=nCP.50  .....(1)

At constant volume

∆Q=nCv∆T ⇒  240=nCv.100......(2)

Equation (1) divided by (2)

160240=CPCV·50100

CPCV=43=1+2f

f=6

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For both the gases, it follows that

PAVAPBVB=nARTAnBRTB   ...1

Given VA=VB and TA=TB.

Thus, from equation (1), it follows that

PAPB=nAnB=12132=16

questions.solution:

So, λ∝T

1500dλ'=273373

questions.q: A gas mixture consists of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn></math> moles of argon and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn></math> moles of oxygen at temperature <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>T</mi></math>. Neglecting all vibrational modes, the total internal energy of the system is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, internal energy is given by, U=nCvT. Also argon gas is monoatomic and oxygen gas is diatomic.

Therefore, total internal energy will beUnet=n1CV1T+n2CV2T

=8×3R2×T+6×5R2×T

=27RT

questions.solution:
RMS speed of O2 gas is vrms=3RTM=3RT32 and most probable speed of O2 gas is vmost probable=2RTM=2RT32.

Here temperature is same.

Thus, vrmsvmost probable=3RT322RT32=32

Hence, vrms=32vp

questions.q: The average kinetic energy of a molecule of the gas is
options: dependent on the nature of the gas
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The average kinetic energy of a molecule of the gas  =32RT.

Average kinetic energy of one molecule of gas =32kT    ( k=RNA)

Where k is Boltzmann constant and T is absolute temperature.

So, from above relation we can say average kinetic energy of molecule is directly proportional to absolute temperature.

questions.q: Consider a gas of triatomic molecules. The molecules  are assumed to be triangular and made of massless rigid rods whose vertices are occupied by atoms. The internal energy of a mole of the gas at temperature T is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula of internal energy of a gas is given by

U=f2RT

Here R is the gas constant and T is temperature.

R=8.314 J mol-1 K-1

For the given configuration of triatomic molecules, the degree of freedom f=6

⇒ U=62RT=3RT

questions.q: During an adiabatic process, if the pressure of a gas is found to be proportional to the cube of its absolute temperature, then the ratio of $\frac{C_{\mathrm{P}}}{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{V}}}$ for the gas is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{P} \propto \mathrm{T}^3 \\
& \mathrm{PT}^{-3}=\text { constant } \\
& \because \frac{\mathrm{PV}}{\mathrm{T}}=\mathrm{nR}=\text { constant from ideal gas equation } \\
& (\mathrm{P})(\mathrm{PV})^{-3}=\text { constant } \\
& \mathrm{P}^{-2} \mathrm{~V}^{-3}=\text { cosntant }...(i)
\end{aligned}\because$ Process equation for adiabatic process is
$\mathrm{PV}^{\mathrm{y}}=\text { constant }...(ii)$
Comparing equation (1) and (2)
$\frac{C_P}{C_V}=y=\frac{3}{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The average time taken by a moving particle between successive collisions or impacts is referred to as the mean free time τ.

The average distance a moving particle travels between successive collisions or impacts is referred to as the mean free path λ.

λ=kT2πd2P

and vrms=3RTM

So, the mean free time τ=λvrms

Therefore, τ∝1T

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I :The average momentum of a molecule in a sample of an ideal gas depends on temperature.

Statement II : The rms speed of oxygen molecules in a gas is v. If the temperature is doubled and the oxygen molecules dissociate into oxygen atoms, the rms speed will become 2v.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Momentum is a vector quantity and average momentum of molecules of a sample is zero due to random motion.

Pavg =0

RMS speed of a molecule is given by

vrms=3RTM

Now the temperature is doubled Tnew =2T and due to dissociation Mnew=M2.

⇒vnew v=2TM2TM

⇒vnew=2v

questions.q:
According to kinetic theory of gases,

A. The motion of the gas molecules freezes at 0°C.

B. The mean free path of gas molecules decreases if the density of molecules is increased.

C. The mean free path of gas molecules increases if temperature is increased keeping pressure constant.

D. Average kinetic energy per molecule per degree of freedom is 32kBT (for monoatomic gases).

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to kinetic theory of gases,

A. The motion of the gas molecules freezes at 0 K.

B. The mean free path decreases on increasing the number density of the molecules.

C. The mean free path increases on increasing the volume. Now if temperature is increased by keeping the pressure constant the volume should increase that is mean free path increases. 

Mean free path λ=12πd2n, here, n=NV

⇒λ=12πd2NV

Using, PV=NKT

⇒λ=KT2πd2P 

D. Average kinetic energy per molecule per degree of freedom is 12kBT.

Thus, B and C only.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a diatomic molecule, the rotational energy at a given temperature obeys Maxwell's distribution.

Statement II : In a diatomic molecule, the rotational energy at a given temperature equals the translational kinetic energy for each molecule.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> is false but Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> is true.
Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> is true but Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> is false.
Both Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> and Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> are true.
Both Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> and Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> are false.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The translational kinetic energy & rotational kinetic energy both obey Maxwell's distribution
independent of each other.
Translational kinetic energy of diatomic molecules =32kT
Rotational kinetic energy of diatomic molecules =22kT
So statement I is true but statement II is false.

questions.q: A metal ball of mass $0.1 \mathrm{~kg}$ is heated upto $500^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and dropped into a vessel of heat capacity $800 \mathrm{JK}^{-1}$ and containing $0.5 \mathrm{~kg}$ water. The initial temperature of water and vessel is $30^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. What is the approximate percentage increment in the temperature of the water? [Specific Heat Capacities of water and metal are, respectively, $4200 \mathrm{Jkg}^{-}{ }^{1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}$ and $400 \mathrm{Jkg}^{-1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}$ ]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Assume final temperature $=\mathrm{T}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ Heat lass $=$ Heat gain $=\mathrm{ms} \Delta \mathrm{T}\Rightarrow \mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{B}} \mathrm{s}_{\mathrm{B}} \Delta \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{B}}=\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{w}} \mathrm{s}_{\mathrm{w}} \Delta \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{w}}0.1 \times 400 \times(500-\mathrm{T})\quad=0.5 \times 4200 \times(\mathrm{T}-30)+800(\mathrm{~T}-30)\Rightarrow 40(500-\mathrm{T})=(\mathrm{T}-30)(2100+800)\Rightarrow 20000-40 \mathrm{~T}=2900 \mathrm{~T}-30 \times 2900\Rightarrow 20000+30 \times 2900=\mathrm{T}(2940)\mathrm{T}=30.4^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\frac{\Delta \mathrm{T}}{\mathrm{T}} \times 100=\frac{6.4}{30} \times 100=21 \%$

so the closest answer is $20 \%$.
